spacr.ops_decode.calibrate_fdr_scale.signature: counts, shuffled, nuclei, sites, axes: Sequence[Tuple[str, Sequence[float]]], *, k: int, scale: float, ci: bool=True, max_rounds: int=20, method: str='shuffle', never=None, **options: Any
spacr.ops_decode.calibrate_fdr_scale.before:
Tune one well's thresholds with the FDR scale set from the shuffle control (item 949).

A decoy sits two or more edits from every barcode, so it misses the
reads that land one edit from a guide, and with short prefixes the decoy
FDR then runs below the barcode-shuffle call rate. Here the scale is
raised until the shuffle call rate is at most
:data:`SHUFFLE_FDR_RATIO` times the calibrated FDR on the tuning
fields: :func:`tune_thresholds` chooses at the current scale; at the
chosen setting the scale needed is the tuning fields' shuffle call rate
over 1.5 times the scale-1 FDR (the upper end of its 95 %
field-bootstrap interval with ``ci``); while that exceeds the current
scale the scale becomes it and the tuner chooses again. The scale only
rises, so the loop ends. Only decoy and shuffle calls are read, never a
reference call set, and the report fields are not used.

:param counts: ``(fields, *axis lengths, 2)`` real and decoy calls.
:param shuffled: ``(fields, *axis lengths)`` shuffle-called cells (a
    mean over the shuffled whitelists).
:param nuclei: cells per field.
:param sites: the site of each field.
:param axes: ``(name, values)`` per axis, as :func:`tune_thresholds`
    takes them.
:param k: decoys per guide.
:param scale: the entered FDR scale; the calibrated scale is never
    below it (nor below 1).
:param ci: judge the tuner's FDR and the needed scale by the upper end
    of their intervals.
:param max_rounds: the most tuner passes.
:param options: the other :func:`tune_thresholds` keywords.
:returns: :func:`tune_thresholds`'s result at the calibrated scale,
    with ``fdr_scale`` and ``calibration``: ``method`` ('shuffle'),
    ``ratio``, ``entered_scale``, ``scale``, ``rounds`` (per pass the
    scale, the setting chosen and the scale it needed), ``converged``,
    and per part (``tune``, ``report``, ``all_fields``)
    :func:`shuffle_call_rate` at the chosen setting with the
    calibrated ``fdr_per_100``, ``shuffle_limit_pct`` (1.5 times it)
    and ``passes`` (rate at or below the limit, to a relative 1e-9).
:raises ValueError: when ``shuffled`` is not the grid of ``counts``.
spacr.ops_decode.calibrate_fdr_scale.source:
Tune one well with a scale measured by shuffle or never-barcode controls.

The existing shuffle method only raises the entered scale until its
call-rate check passes. Never calibration measures wrong library calls
from substitution-control opportunities and may lower or raise the
scale, with a floor of one. Both methods use this loop and the same
threshold tuner. A repeated never setting ends the loop; a cycle keeps
the larger tested cycling scale and its matching threshold result.
The report half is held out from never calibration.

:param counts: ``(fields, *axis lengths, 2)`` real and decoy calls.
:param shuffled: matching shuffle-call grid, or None without shuffle.
:param nuclei: cells per field.
:param sites: each field site.
:param axes: axis names and values passed to ``tune_thresholds``.
:param k: positive matched-decoy multiplicity.
:param scale: entered scale; shuffle cannot lower it, never can.
:param ci: choose the upper field-bootstrap scale and tuner intervals.
:param max_rounds: maximum tuner passes, default 20.
:param method: none, shuffle (the compatibility default), never or
    never+shuffle, which takes the larger of the two measured scales.
:param never: mapping of ``never2_calls``, ``opp2_N2``, ``opp2_L`` and
    optional ``never1_calls``, ``opp1_N1``, ``opp1_L`` field/grid arrays.
    Entry points also supply ``library_size`` for the 50-guide guard,
    ``never_sets`` metadata and optional N1/N2 real-call grids.
    Fewer than 30 tuning-half N2 calls keep the entered scale.
:param options: other ``tune_thresholds`` keywords.
:returns: the tuner result with ``fdr_scale`` and ``calibration``.
    Shuffle keeps its existing ratio, per-part call-rate checks and
    round structure. Never adds point/interval estimates for each
    half, entered-scale FDR, status, control metadata and perturbation
    changes. Production calls are never replaced by control calls.
:raises ValueError: for an unknown method, invalid grid shape, missing
    never arrays or fewer than one permitted tuner pass.

spacr.ops_decode.never_scale.signature: real, decoy, never2_calls, opp2_N2, opp2_L, *, k, ci=True, reps=_AUTO_REPS, seed=_AUTO_BOOT_SEED, never1_calls=None, opp1_N1=None, opp1_L=None
spacr.ops_decode.never_scale.source:
Estimate the decoy FDR scale from calls on substitution-built controls.

The N2 call rate per distance-two opportunity predicts wrong library
calls at that distance. Libraries containing distance-one guide pairs
also contribute the N1 rate times their distance-one opportunities.
The expected wrong calls times k, divided by the observed decoy calls,
give the scale. A zero decoy sum uses ``_AUTO_ZERO_DECOYS``, as the
existing threshold tuner does. With ci, the chosen scale is the upper
end of the 95 percent field bootstrap, using the existing row sampler.
Clipping the chosen scale to one belongs to ``calibrate_fdr_scale``.

:param real: real production calls per field at one grid setting.
:param decoy: production decoy calls in the same fields.
:param never2_calls: calls on the distance-two control set.
:param opp2_N2: production guide counts times their N2 distance-two neighbours.
:param opp2_L: the corresponding other-library distance-two opportunities.
:param k: positive matched-decoy multiplicity.
:param ci: choose the upper bootstrap scale rather than its point estimate.
:param reps: bootstrap draws, default the existing ``_AUTO_REPS``.
:param seed: field-bootstrap seed, default ``_AUTO_BOOT_SEED``.
:param never1_calls: optional distance-one control calls per field.
:param opp1_N1: N1 distance-one opportunities; supplied with never1_calls.
:param opp1_L: other-library distance-one opportunities, otherwise zero.
:returns: dict with ``scale``, ``scale_point``, ``scale_ci95``, ``rho1``,
    ``rho2``, ``rho1_over_rho2``, ``fdr_cal_pct``, their ``*_ci95``
    intervals, ``expected_wrong`` and summed real/decoy/control counts.
    Intervals are None for fewer than two fields. Rates with no
    control opportunities and estimates depending on them are None;
    a ratio with zero rho2 is also unavailable.
:raises ValueError: for misaligned, negative or nonfinite counts, a
    nonpositive multiplicity, or incomplete N1 inputs.

spacr.ops_prefix.run_prefix_decode.before:
The ``prefix_decode`` phase: decode every indexed site against spacer prefixes.

Reads the cropped-site layout (item 919, ``ops_layout='cpg_cropped'``),
builds the whitelist, decodes each complete site's sequencing stack
(cycles 1 to the prefix's last cycle), takes each read's cell from
``ops_prefix_masks`` (or the site's ``merged/`` labels), calls cells and
writes, under ``<dst_root>/results/ops_prefix/``:

* ``library_prefix_collisions.csv`` and ``library_summary.json``;
* ``quality_classes.json`` (the quality method, its class definitions
  and the settings);
* ``reads_<plate>_<well_id>.parquet`` (one row per read) and
  ``cells_<plate>_<well_id>.csv`` (:func:`prefix_cell_calls`);
* ``site_summary.csv`` (per site: :func:`read_fractions`, cells with
  reads, cells with an exact read, cells per class);
* ``cells_per_guide.csv`` and ``cells_per_gene.csv`` (perfect and great
  cells);
* with decoys (``ops_prefix_decoy_k`` above 0, item 942): a ``decoy``
  column in the cell tables (a decoy call keeps its prefix but no
  genotype), ``cells_in_labels``, ``cells_real``, ``cells_decoy`` and
  ``fdr_pct`` in ``site_summary.csv``, and ``fdr_<plate>_<well_id>.json``
  (:func:`spacr.ops_decode.fdr_report`);
* with ``ops_prefix_threshold_tuning`` 'per_well_decoy': per well
  ``threshold_tuning_<plate>_<well_id>.csv`` and ``.png`` (every grid
  setting's tuning numbers and the genotyped-vs-FDR curve,
  :func:`spacr.ops_decode.write_tuning_curve`) and ``.json`` (the choice,
  :func:`spacr.ops_decode.tune_thresholds`); each site's spots are found
  once, down to the lowest read threshold, and the chosen setting's reads
  and cells are written;
* with near-miss decoys (``ops_prefix_nearmiss_decoy_k`` above 0, item
  949, :func:`prefix_nearmiss_decoys`): a ``decoy_class`` column
  (``'far'`` or ``'nearmiss'``) in the cell tables,
  ``cells_decoy_nearmiss`` and ``fdr_nearmiss_pct`` (near-miss calls per
  100 real calls over ``ops_prefix_nearmiss_decoy_k``, scale 1) in
  ``site_summary.csv``, and the near-miss count, FDR and its interval in
  ``fdr_<plate>_<well_id>.json``; ``cells_decoy`` and ``fdr_pct`` keep
  counting the far decoys only;
* with ``ops_prefix_fdr_calibration`` 'shuffle' (item 949): every read is
  also matched against :data:`spacr.ops_decode.SHUFFLE_SEEDS` shuffled
  whitelists (:func:`shuffled_library`, seeds ``ops_control_seed`` and
  up), and each well's FDR scale is raised from that control
  (:func:`spacr.ops_decode.calibrate_fdr_scale`; without tuning at the
  entered setting); ``fdr_pct`` uses the calibrated scale, and
  ``site_summary.csv`` gains ``shuffle_called`` (mean over the shuffled
  whitelists), ``shuffle_call_rate_pct`` and ``fdr_scale``; the FDR
  report gains the entered scale, the calibration, the FDR's interval
  and the shuffle call rate with its interval
  (:func:`spacr.ops_decode.shuffle_call_rate`). With both item-949
  settings off the outputs are those of item 942;
* with ``ops_prefix_minority_min_reads`` 2 or more (item 967, alpha): the
  cell calls and the tuning leave out minority stray reads
  (:func:`prefix_cell_calls`), the cell table gains
  ``minority_ignored`` and ``minority_rescued``, ``site_summary.csv``
  gains ``cells_minority_rescued`` (genotyped cells called only because
  of the rule), and one line per well reports the rescued cells. 0, the
  default, writes what the run wrote before;
* with ``ops_prefix_quality_method`` 'weighted_majority' (item 988,
  alpha): cells are called by their barcodes' summed read weights
  (:func:`prefix_cell_calls`, classes :data:`WEIGHTED_CLASSES`), the
  tuning also tries the weight axes (:data:`WEIGHT_GRID_KEYS`;
  :data:`PREFIX_TUNING_GRID_WEIGHTED` when the grid is empty), and the
  cell table gains the weight columns. With a distance term the read
  table gains ``nuc_gap_px`` and ``nuc_gap_fallback``, measured to the
  nuclei of ``ops_prefix_nuclei_masks``;
* with ``ops_keep_multi_guide_cells`` (item 988, alpha): per well
  ``guide_multiplicity_<plate>_<well_id>.csv`` (the share of cells by
  number of guides, and the share of two-guide cells whose runner-up is
  a touching cell's top guide) and ``multi_guide_cells_<plate>_<well_id>.csv``
  (the cells with two or more guides of ``ops_multi_guide_min_reads``
  reads, none of them from a neighbour). With both item-988 settings
  off the run writes what it wrote before.
* with ``ops_prefix_tuning_min_sites`` above 0 (item 982 small-well
  guard, alpha): a tuned well with fewer sites keeps the read-quality
  floor at :data:`SMALL_WELL_FLOOR` and tunes only the other settings;
  the log says so, and the well's tuning json and ``tuning`` entry gain
  ``small_well_floor`` and ``small_well_sites``. 0, the default, writes
  what the run wrote before.

:param settings: the OPS settings: ``dst_root``, the ``cpg_*`` reader
    settings, the item-920, item-942, item-949, item-967 and item-988
    settings
    (:func:`prefix_settings`)
    and, for tuning, the shared tuner's settings
    (``ops_decode_auto_objective``, ``ops_decode_auto_f_beta``,
    ``ops_decode_auto_unreachable``, ``ops_decode_auto_ci``,
    ``ops_decode_auto_tune_fraction`` and ``ops_decode_auto_seed``).
:param report: called with progress lines.
:returns: the output paths, the library summary and the run's totals;
    with any item-942 setting on also ``seconds_per_well``, ``fdr`` (per
    well) and ``tuning`` (per well: the choice and its numbers); with
    the shuffle calibration also ``calibration`` (per well); with the
    minority-read rule (item 967) also ``minority_rescued`` (genotyped
    cells rescued, per well); with ``ops_keep_multi_guide_cells`` (item
    988) also ``multi_guide`` (per well: the two table paths and the
    number of multi-guide cells); with tuning also ``well_choices``, one
    line per well (item 966): the read mode and thresholds chosen and
    the decoy FDR on the tuning and the report sites, also sent to
    ``report`` last. An empty ``ops_read_mode`` is
    ``'auto'`` with tuning and ``'log'`` without.
:raises ValueError: without ``dst_root`` or a library, when the layout
    has fewer sequencing cycles than the prefix needs, for tuning,
    near-miss decoys or a shuffle calibration without decoys, or for a
    distance term or the touching cells without the labels they need.

Substitution-built barcodes that no cell in the guide library should carry.

Distance-one controls have exactly one nearest guide and use a different
substituted position for each accepted control of that guide.
Distance-two controls have no guide at distance zero or one. Every
control lies at least two substitutions from previously accepted and
excluded controls. Sorted unique guides are visited round by round,
with one seeded generator and up to 200 attempts per guide and round.
The same builder serves full-barcode and sequenced-prefix calibration.

    columns count control or other-library barcodes at distances 1–3.

:raises ValueError: for an unsupported distance, negative or fractional
    k or seed, or a barcode containing letters outside A/C/G/T.

runtime_sources.key: ops_decode_fdr_calibration
runtime_sources.source: How rule (a) sets the FDR scale. 'never' measures error calls on substitution-built barcodes through the same read and pixel votes: distance-two controls set the scale and distance-one controls report a check. It can raise or lower the entered scale, down to 1. Manual thresholds stay fixed while calibration runs. 'none' keeps ops_fdr_scale; 'shuffle' only raises it from three shuffled libraries; 'never+shuffle' takes the larger control-based scale. Never methods need decoys and keep the entered scale when evidence is insufficient. Default 'never'.
runtime_sources.before: How auto thresholds set the FDR scale. 'none' uses ops_fdr_scale as entered. 'shuffle' also votes every field against three shuffled copies of the library and raises the scale until the shuffled libraries' call rate is at most 1.5 times the FDR on the tuning fields, then tunes again at that scale. The scale used and the shuffle call rate go into the threshold and FDR reports. Costs about three more vote passes per field. Default 'none'. Alpha.

runtime_sources.key: ops_fdr_scale
runtime_sources.source: Entered multiplier for the decoy FDR after accounting for decoys per guide. This is the starting scale and fallback when calibration has too little evidence; 'none' keeps it fixed. Values below 1 count as 1. The Funk library reference value is 1.268. Default 1.268.
runtime_sources.before: How much likelier a read is to land on a wrong real guide than on a decoy, which turns decoy calls into an FDR. 1.268 was measured for the Funk et al. 2022 library from its guides' neighbour distances; values below 1 count as 1. Default 1.268.

runtime_sources.key: ops_prefix_fdr_calibration
runtime_sources.source: Set the spacer-prefix FDR scale. 'never' measures substitution-built controls through the production matcher and votes; distance-two controls set the scale and distance-one controls provide a check. Fixed thresholds stay fixed. 'none' keeps the earlier uncalibrated tables and reports no shuffles. 'shuffle' only raises the scale; 'never+shuffle' takes the larger control-based scale. Never and shuffle methods report shuffle rates. Without decoys, never methods keep the entered scale. Default 'never'.
runtime_sources.before: How the spacer-prefix decode sets its FDR scale. 'none' uses ops_prefix_fdr_scale as entered. 'shuffle' also matches every read against three shuffled whitelists and raises the scale until the shuffle call rate is at most 1.5 times the FDR on the tuning sites, then tunes again at that scale. The scale and the shuffle call rate go into site_summary.csv and the FDR report. Needs ops_prefix_decoy_k above 0. Default 'none'. Alpha.

runtime_sources.key: ops_prefix_fdr_scale
runtime_sources.source: Entered multiplier for the decoy FDR after accounting for decoys per prefix. This is the starting scale and fallback when calibration has too little evidence; 'none' keeps it fixed. Values below 1 count as 1. Default 1. Alpha.
runtime_sources.before: How much likelier a read is to land on a wrong guide than on a decoy prefix, which turns decoy calls into an FDR; values below 1 count as 1. No calibration exists for spacer-prefix libraries yet. Default 1. Alpha.

The existing one-deletion index supplies the distance-one matches.
Two- and three-deletion signatures count the other distances without
constructing the guide-by-barcode distance matrix. One signature
position set is held at a time. A pair at distance h contributes
``choose(length - h, d - h)`` signatures of order d; subtracting the
lower-distance terms therefore gives exact Hamming counts.

:param guides: sorted unique guide strings, including mixed lengths.
:param barcodes: sorted unique strings whose distances are counted.
:returns: read-only int64 ``(guides, 3)`` array, columns distances 1–3;
    exact matches, including a guide itself, are excluded.

private_and_test_docs.source:
Give a file the defaults of the version it was written under.

WHY (item 931). A saved settings file or run journal must give the same
result when it is run again, but a file only holds the keys that existed
when it was written. When a later release changes a default, a key the
file never set would silently take the NEW default. Every file spaCR
writes therefore carries ``SETTINGS_VERSION_KEY`` =
``SETTINGS_SCHEMA_VERSION``, and ``DEFAULT_CHANGES`` says, per version,
what a key's default was BEFORE that version. A file with no stamp --
hand-written or older than the stamp -- is read as the oldest version
and gets every old default listed, with a logged notice naming each one
and how to take today's default instead.

TO CHANGE A DEFAULT: add one row to ``DEFAULT_CHANGES``, keyed by the
item number that changes it and holding the OLD default, and raise
``SETTINGS_SCHEMA_VERSION`` to that number. The key must be above every
existing key, because files are already stamped with the current
version; an item whose number is lower takes the next free number and
is listed under that number in docs/source/reproducibility_manifests.rst.
A format-only change instead adds its version to
``SETTINGS_FORMAT_VERSIONS`` and leaves ``DEFAULT_CHANGES`` unchanged.
Version 950 records exact resolved parameters without changing defaults.
933 is item 930's switch of ``ops_align_model`` to ``'tile_affine'``:
it landed after 932, so it could not take 930. 934 is item 937's
``aggregation_defaults`` ``'per_feature'`` (the screen pipeline's
per-feature well table); older files keep ``'legacy'``.
935 is item 940's switch of ``ops_placement_seed_export`` to True: every
solved stitch writes a placement file, and files stamped before keep
it off.
936 is the OPS stage-3 Hybrid profile's ``ops_blas_threads`` (2, was
1) and ``ops_consensus_space`` (``'hybrid'``, was ``'refit'``).
937 is item 941's removal of Gabor and colocalisation from the
``'profiling'`` preset of ``profile_features`` and
``ops_ph_profile_features``: files stamped before get
``profile_optional_families`` and ``ops_ph_profile_optional_families``
with the three families ``'profiling'`` measured then, so their columns
are unchanged.
938 is item 945's ``seg_mask_vram_gb``: the
large-site mask step is sized to 6 GB of card memory, and files stamped
before keep 0, no cap of its own.
940 is item 946's switch of the OPS decode to the proven Funk decode:
``ops_decode_preset`` ``'rule_a_s2'`` (was ``'none'``) and
``ops_decode_threshold_mode`` ``'auto'`` (was ``'manual'``), with
``ops_decode_auto_spot_grid`` back to ``[]`` (calling thresholds only;
files stamped 939 keep item 942's joint grid).
943 is item 965's large-site nuclei (R2): ``seg_cells_from_nucleus_seeds``
``True`` (was ``False``) and ``seg_merge_small_nuclei_frac`` ``0.25``
(was ``0.0``); files stamped before keep the cell model's own cells
and no merge, so their labels are unchanged.
944 is item 966's spacer-prefix decode default: ``ops_read_mode``
empty, which that decode reads as ``'auto'`` while it tunes (was
``'log'``), ``ops_prefix_threshold_tuning`` ``'per_well_decoy'`` (was
``'none'``), ``ops_prefix_decoy_k`` 4 (was 0) and
``ops_prefix_fdr_target_pct`` 1.0 (was 0.1); files stamped before keep
the fixed thresholds and the log read, and the OPS barcode decode reads
an empty ``ops_read_mode`` as ``'log'`` either way.
945 is item 987b's automatic ``batch_size`` of Make Masks (0, the largest
batch that fits the free GPU and RAM; was 50): files stamped before keep
50, so their masks, normalised per batch, are unchanged.
947 is item 967's minority-read rule on the spacer-prefix decode:
``ops_prefix_minority_min_reads`` 3 (was 0, off); files stamped before
keep 0, so every barcode of a cell counts in its call as before.
948 is TASK X's routing of OPS Cellpose through the shared mask tile
batch (``mask_eval_batch_size``; 0 is one tile per field in the resident
batch). Files stamped before get the tile batches the OPS paths always
ran at: ``ops_ph_tile_batch`` 8 (the phenotype path's
``ops_ph_batch_size``, which an old file that sets it keeps, since it is
renamed to this key), ``ops_sbs_tile_batch`` 16 (stitched sequencing
nuclei) and ``spatial_tile_batch`` 16 (Spatial Mask Generation). 946 and
947 belong to other items, so this takes 948.

957 adds automatic FDR-scale calibration from never-should-appear
barcodes (item 1014, method ``'never'``). Files stamped before keep
the entered fixed scale (``'none'``).

:param settings: the file's settings under today's names, edited in
    place.
:param version: the file's schema version from
    :func:`_settings_file_version`; 0 for an unstamped file.
:param known: the keys the pipeline being run reads, or None for any key.
    A row for another pipeline's key is not added to this one's settings.
:returns: ``key -> (old default, version that changed it)`` for every key
    filled in. A key the file sets is never touched. When a key changed
    more than once, the default of the earliest change after ``version``
    is the one the file was written under. An explicit legacy
    ``crop_source`` supplies a missing ``image_source`` before its old
    default is inserted, preserving the requested source mode.

private_and_test_docs.source:
The user-facing setting keys.

``settings.py``'s ``tooltips`` and ``expected_types``, PLUS the EN i18n
catalog's ``SETTING_TOOLTIPS``. Declared OPS tooltips also supply
their keys before a generated catalog has caught up.

WHY THE CATALOG IS NEEDED. A module may declare its own settings
locally: `hit_investigation_default_settings` builds a `tips` dict
inside the function body, so 17 `hit_*` settings appear in the
Investigate Hit panel and in no module-scope table. This function
scanned only module scope in one file, so it did not know they were
settings, so nothing that read them counted as a read, so their API
links had no target. They were not rare or obscure -- they are most
of one module's panel.

The catalog is the right second source because it is the list of
settings the GUI actually shows: it is generated from the resolved
runtime tables, so a setting a user can see is in it by
construction, wherever its tooltip was declared.

private_and_test_docs.source:
Setting tooltip sources, read with `ast` rather than imported.

Declared OPS help fills gaps without replacing existing catalog or
global-setting text.

IMPORTING IT WOULD HAVE BEEN ONE LINE and it broke the tool's central
promise: everything here is pure `ast`, so a broken import cannot
quietly empty the trees, and the docs build needs no torch, no Qt and
no GPU. `spacr.settings` pulls all three. The suite has a test on
that invariant and it is the test that caught this.

A literal dict at module scope is exactly what `ast.literal_eval`
exists for, so the cost of keeping the promise is a dozen lines.
Entries whose value is not a plain string -- an f-string, a
concatenation, a name -- are skipped rather than guessed at.
